classification_policy: One record per individual email message. Thread grouping is synthetic and contains no Gmail identifiers. Public repository notifications retain public repository context. Account-security and private workspace messages are individually classified but redacted. Email claims never become verified CI, review, admission, or merge state.

record_taxonomy.INSIGHT: Create only after independent corroboration and human review.
record_taxonomy.KEYWORDS: Repository IDs, workflow names, commit prefixes and tags are metadata facets, not primary record kinds.

collection.label_filter: No Gmail label filter was applied; this is a broader GitHub-sender snapshot, not a verified export of the Gmail 'git reviews' label.
limitations: Gmail search returns threads; every message is represented separately and grouped by a synthetic thread_group key.
No raw Gmail message/thread IDs, email addresses, bodies, unsubscribe URLs, tokens, OAuth application names, PAT names, authentication codes, or private workspace identifiers are published.
Only public repository subjects and message dates are retained; private account/workspace messages are individually classified but redacted.
Workflow conclusions and review outcomes must be corroborated against GitHub API resources and exact commit/run IDs.
This snapshot is not a live ingestion feed; do not use it as the canonical archive or operational state store.

engineering-intelligence: Canonical evidence atlas and ADR registry; no automatic admission authority.

twgt-schema-gate: Canonical boundary schemas and dual-runtime validation.
twgt-bridge: Read-only evidence collector; current harvest workflow conflicts with README by pushing evidence automatically.
twgt-git-hitl: Human review surface; no automated admission authority.
agentnotebooklm: Research app and proposed review archive; not canonical governance owner.
opa: Policy-engine dependency/mirror; deployed policy state requires independent verification.
temporal: Workflow orchestration candidate; CI does not prove TWGT runtime adoption.
